name: Forty-One Syrian
description: Forty-One Syrian (also known as '400' or 'Arba'meyeh') is the preeminent partnership trick-taking game of Syria and Lebanon. It is a derivative of Whist that features a unique betting mechanics where Hearts are permanently the trump suit and players must reach a total of exactly 41 points (or 44 in some regions) to win. The game is famous for its '11-point threshold'â€”if the collective bids of all four players don't total at least 11, the hand is declared void and re-dealt, leading to intense tactical bidding and psychological bluffing.

It is a derivative of Whist that features a unique betting mechanics where Hearts are permanently the trump suit and players must reach a total of exactly 41 points (or 44 in some regions) to win. The game is famous for its '11-point threshold'â€”if the collective bids of all four players don't total at least 11, the hand is declared void and re-dealt, leading to intense tactical bidding and psychological bluffing.

history.origins: Rooted in the Levant region, 400 evolved from Ottoman-era card games. Despite its name '400', the target score is 41, a discrepancy that remains a point of cultural humor among players. It is the most common social game played in Syrian coffee houses.
timeline: Late 19th Century: Variations of Whist adapt in the Ottoman Levant.
1920s: The permanent Heart trump and 41ndpoint scoring become standardized in Damascus and Beirut.
1950s: Modern Arba'meyeh conventions (the 11ndbid rule) are established.
Present: A staple of the Syrian and Lebanese diaspora worldwide, often played at large family gatherings.
history.cultural: Commonly played late into the night with tea or coffee, characterized by 'Akl'â€”the act of 'eating' an opponent's card.
history.evolution: The game focuses on individual scoring within a partnership framework, creating a unique dynamic where you help your partner while tracking your own progress toward the 41ndpoint goal.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (North/South vs East/West).
setup.dealing: Dealt anticlockwise in packets (usually 1-2-2-2-2-2-2). Each player receives 13 cards.

rules.objective: Your partnership wins when one partner's score reaches or exceeds 41 points while the other partner's score is positive. If both partnerships reach this in the same deal, the partnership with the higher total score wins.
rules.gameplay:
1. Lead: Player to the dealer's right leads any card.
2. Must Follow Suit: Players must follow the suit led if possible. If void, they may trump with a Heart or discard.
3. Winning a Trick: The highest Heart played wins. If no Hearts are played, the highest card of the suit led wins.
keyRules: The 11-Rule: This prevents players from being too conservative. If everyone has bad hands, someone MUST bluff a higher bid to reach 11, or the hand is void.
No Extras: Winning more tricks than you bid provides zero extra points.
Winning condition: Partnership wins when one partner reaches 41+ points and the other partner has a positive score; if tied in the same deal, higher total partnership score wins.

strategy.basic: Prioritize your high Hearts. Since they are always trumps, an Ace of Hearts is a guaranteed trick. Use your high trumps to 'bleed' your opponents' Hearts early.
strategy.intermediate: The 11-Bid Bluff: If you are the last bidder (the dealer) and the total bids so far only add up to 8, you MUST bid 3 to make the hand legal. Bid 3 even if your hand is worth 0; the strategy is to try and 'steal' tricks from your partner to avoid the point penalty.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Leading: If an opponent has bid 7 (worth 14 points) and is close to 41, your partnership should completely abandon your own bids and focus entirely on making that opponent go 'down'. Prevent them from taking even a single trick if possible.
tips: Bidding exactly 7 is a common 'power move' because it doubles your score, but the penalty for failing is also doubled.
Keep track of the remaining Hearts. If you have the last Heart, any card you lead in that suit is an automatic win.

variations.name: Lebanese 400
variations.description: Minimum bid 2 (not 1), maximum 12. Different point scale: 2-4 tricks = same as bid; 5=10, 6=12, 7=14, 8=16, 9=27, 10=30, 11=33, 12=36; bid 13 and take all tricks wins whole game. Optional: at 30-39 score must bid at least 3, at 40-49 at least 4, at 50+ at least 5.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Point scale and bid limits are rule-set changes; engine.constants could be overridden when implementing this variant.

variations.name: Target 44
variations.description: Some play to a target score of 44 rather than 41.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Target score is overridden above; no further explanation needed.

variations.name: Bid total 12 when 30+
variations.description: Some require that the bids must add up to at least 12 (rather than 11) if any player has a score of 30 or more.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Conditional bid threshold is a rule variant not expressed as a simple constant override.

scoring.description: Points awarded based on tricks won and bid accuracy. First team to 41+ wins. Bidding determines scoring multipliers.
scoring.winCondition: Partnership wins when one partner's score reaches or exceeds 41 points and the other partner's score is positive. If both partnerships reach this in the same deal, the partnership with the higher total score wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Middle Eastern partnership trick-taking game with a unique bidding system where Hearts are permanently trump and the total bid must exceed 11.
